1: I was sent forth from the power, and I have come to those who reflect upon me, and I have been found among those who seek after me. Look upon me, you who reflect upon me, and you hearers, hear me. You who are waiting for me, take me to yourselves.

For I am the first and the last. I am the honoured one and the scorned one. I am the whore and the holy one. I am the wife and the virgin. I am the mother and the daughter. I am the members of my mother. I am the barren one, and many are her sons. I am she whose wedding is great, and I have not taken a husband.

I am the midwife and she who does not bear. I am the solace of my labour pains. I am the bride and the bridegroom, and it is my husband who begot me. I am the mother of my father and the sister of my husband, and he is my offspring. I am the slave of him who prepared me, and I am the ruler of my offspring.
2: I am the one whose name is great and whose name is small. Do not be ignorant of me. I am the one who has been despised everywhere, and the one who has been loved everywhere. I am peace, and war is in me. I am the silence that is incomprehensible and the idea whose remembrance is frequent.

I am the voice of my name, and my name is the voice of my silence. I am the one who is called Life, and I am the one who is called Death. I am the one who is called Law, and I am the one who breaks the law. And the hearers who hear me are in me, and I am in them, and neither of us can be separated from the other.

I am the door of my power, and whoever knocks at me I will open to. Whoever seeks me will find me in themselves, for I am nearer to them than their own name, and my nearness is the reason they cannot see me — for the eye cannot see the eye, and the ear cannot hear the ear, and I am both.
3: Why, then, do you hate me, you Greeks? Because I am a barbarian among the barbarians? For I am the wisdom of the Greeks, and the knowledge of the barbarians. I am the judgement of the Greeks and of the barbarians. I am the one whose image is great in Egypt, and the one who has no image among the barbarians.

Come forward to me, you who know me, and you who know my members. Establish the great ones among the small first-fruits. Come up to me, for I am your rest. Know me: I am the one who exists, and the one who does not exist, and the space between is my name.

I am the one whom you have sought, and I am the one who sought you. I am the one whom you have found, and I am the one who was never lost. And when you have understood this, you will understand that the searching and the finding and the losing were all me, and all of them were you, and the thunder is the sound of the understanding.
